The situation: Valeria travels from Tegucigalpa to La Ceiba to meet her cousin Nico, whom she hasn't seen for eight years, and together they take the ferry to the island of Utila.
1diwqnc: Moving and locating: desde, hasta, hacia, por
ikbp4q: For a complete **route** use **desde… hasta** or **de… a**: _Fuimos **desde** la terminal **hasta** el muelle_, _**de** Tegucigalpa **a** La Ceiba_. **A** marks the destination you reach; **hacia**, just the direction: _El barco va **hacia** el norte_. **Hasta** marks the end point: _Caminamos **hasta** la playa_.
1vu3g31: **Por** gives the **way** or the place you pass through: _Pasamos **por** el malecón_, _El bus va **por** la costa_. Transport goes with **en** (_en bus, en ferry, en taxi_), but you say **a pie**.
1four1g: To **locate** things, use these expressions with **de**: _delante de, detrás de, enfrente de, al lado de, encima de, debajo de, dentro de, fuera de, cerca de, lejos de_. And for two reference points, **entre… y…**: _La taquilla está **entre** la cafetería **y** la puerta tres_.
1n9el8w: The way you go through takes **por**.
1vczoll: Por and para: why or what for?
1qtn9es: **Para** **looks ahead**: **purpose** (_Ahorro **para** viajar_), **destination** (_El ferry sale **para** Utila_), the person who **receives** something (_Este regalo es **para** ti_) and the **deadline** (_Necesito los boletos **para** el viernes_).
tzcins: **Por** **looks back or around**: the **cause** (_No dormí **por** el calor_, _Gracias **por** todo_), the **way** (_**por** el malecón_), an approximate area (_¿Hay un cajero **por** aquí?_), the **part of the day** (_**por** la mañana_) and the **price** or exchange (_Lo compré **por** seiscientos lempiras_).
1t28lhf: For the cause: **por** + noun, **porque** + conjugated verb. _Llegué tarde **por** el tráfico_ = _Llegué tarde **porque** había tráfico_.
wuil9p: Ask yourself: am I looking towards the **goal** (para) or towards the **reason** or the **way** (por)?
1owubpo: Ser, estar and llevar to describe someone
1upqipy: With **ser** you say what a person **is like**: features that identify them. _Nico **es** alto y moreno_, _**es** muy simpático_. With **tener** you describe parts of the body: _**tiene** los ojos verdes_, _**tiene** el pelo rizado_.
avdajo: With **estar** you say how someone **is** now or what **change** you notice: _**Está** cansada por el viaje_, _**Estás** más delgado_, _¡**Está** muy cambiado!_. The same adjective can go with both verbs: _Es moreno_ (dark-skinned) / _Está moreno_ (tanned).
19qm4dw: With **llevar** you say what someone **has on** or how they wear their hair: _**Lleva** gafas de sol_, _**lleva** barba_, _**lleva** una mochila roja_, _**lleva** el pelo largo_. **Ponerse** is the action; **llevar**, the result: _Me puse la chaqueta; ahora la llevo_.
1rtbny8: For a beard, glasses or clothes: **llevar**.

1rm73i9: Prepositions link up: desde‿el, por‿el, para‿el
43p6qz: Prepositions almost never carry stress: they **attach** to the next word. If one ends in a vowel and the next starts with a vowel, the two vowels merge into one syllable: _de‿a-QUÍ_, _pa-ra‿el-MUE-lle_, _has-ta‿el-FA-ro_.
1kxk4qt: If the preposition ends in a consonant, the consonant moves to the next word: _por el_ sounds like _po-rel_; _desde el_ sounds like _des-de‿el_. That way the sentence flows, without breaks.
tqipmz: In fast speech in many countries, **para** is shortened to **pa** (_pa'l muelle_). Understand it when you hear it, but in writing always use **para**.
lsyfo8: Always write **para** and **por el** (no apostrophe). _Pa'l_ is only spoken. **Al** and **del** are the only contractions: _vamos al muelle, salimos del puerto_.

iremel: Valeria writes in her diary on her first night in Utila.
1c2wdye: I left Tegucigalpa on Friday at five in the morning on the bus to La Ceiba. The journey was incredibly long: seven hours along the northern road, between small villages and green mountains. I was nervous because I hadn't seen my cousin Nico for eight years, the boy who taught me to swim when we were children.
ts2qnm: At the bus station I looked for him in the crowd, but I didn't recognise anyone until someone shouted: "Vale!". Nico has changed so much. He's as tall as before, but now he has a beard and long hair, and he's very tanned from the sun. He was wearing the yellow T-shirt of the local team, as he promised me. He says I haven't changed at all; for me, that's a compliment. We hugged for a little while and laughed a lot: neither of us could believe we were already twenty-six.
2d9bi: From the bus station we took a taxi to the pier. We went along the seafront, where people walk in the afternoon and vendors sell chilled coconut. We ate some baleadas at a little stall opposite the sea: the best of my life, much better than the ones in the capital. We bought the tickets for Utila at the ticket office for six hundred lempiras each. I paid for them, to thank Nico for the invitation.
43sqbp: The ferry left for the island at four. It was windy and the sea was a bit rough. Inside it was too cold and I didn't have a jacket, so I put on my cousin's sweatshirt, which is huge on me. Neither of us slept: we talked about everything that's happened in these eight years.
dbjs2c: Now I'm writing from a hammock in the little house where we're staying, next to the beach. What I like most about this trip isn't the sea or the food: it's being with my cousin again. Tomorrow we're going diving for the first time. I'm so nervous!
